item.title: Paramount Settles Lawsuits With States Clearing the Way to Buy WBD
item.description: Paramount Skydance settles lawsuits with 12 states clearing the way for it to buy Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. The deal limits Paramount's market power and it promises to release 30 movies a year at the combined studios. Charlie Pellett has the breaking news. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Tokens Jump Up to 50% in a Post-Clarity Regulatory Bet
item.description: Crypto tokens tied to trading and tokenization are surging after US regulators moved to expand digital-asset markets despite the failure of landmark crypto legislation in Congress.
item.dc:creator: Muyao Shen

item.title: NYC Airports Disrupted by Air Traffic Control Outage
item.description: Flights at New York’s major airports were disrupted after a technical problem at an air traffic control facility in Philadelphia. A so-called ground stop was in effect at John F. Kennedy International, LaGuardia, and Newark Liberty International. Sid Philip reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Radiant World Table Shows Six Lenders With $870 Million Exposure
item.description: Radiant World has disclosed $870 million outstanding to six creditors who financed its receivables, according to a spreadsheet included in a legal filing by the embattled commodity trader.
item.dc:creator: Jack Farchy, Arno Schütze and Thomas Biesheuvel

item.title: Stocks Climb on US-China Optimism, Copper's AI Bppm
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger and Michael Ball on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Stocks rally and oil drops as investors look to diplomacy, with President Trump and China’s Xi Jinping preparing for a high-stakes White House meeting later this week. Plus, inside Anthropic’s new AI safety partnership with Accenture, and Wall Street’s race to manage the risks and rewards of artificial intelligence.And legendary mining investor Robert Friedland joins us on why copper and rare earths are becoming the new front line in the US, China resource race. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paramount Talks Include Penalty for Missing 30-Film Pledge
item.description: Geetha Ranganathan, Bloomberg Intelligence analyst, joined Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu to discuss the latest on the ongoing Paramount and Warner Bros. merger. The settlement talks between Paramount Skydance Corp. and California officials over the planned acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. are said to include a financial penalty if the company fails to make good on a promise to distribute 30 films per year in theaters. Paramount would have to pay $30 million for each film that falls short of that goal, according to two people familiar with the discussions who asked to not be identified because the negotiations are private. It could also be forced to sell its stake in Miramax, the studio behind movies such as Pulp Fiction, if it fails to meet the target, one of the people said. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Drops Below $100 With Focus on Hormuz Flows, Diplomacy
item.description: Rob Barnett, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Energy and Commodities Analyst, joined Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu to discuss the latest in oil. Oil fell below $100, heading for its longest run of declines since June, as robust flows through the Strait of Hormuz and diplomacy around the US-Iran war tamed a recent rally. Brent, the global benchmark, fell as much as 4.2% while West Texas Intermediate futures were down over 5% to trade near $95 a barrel. Satellite data showed that Saudi Arabia’s observed oil loadings from inside the Persian Gulf jumped over the weekend, with the highest number of ships seen at the nation’s main Persian Gulf port since June. It’s a sign the kingdom has pivoted back toward Hormuz after the shutdown of a key cross-country pipeline to the Red Sea earlier this month following drone attacks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gabon Plans $2 Billion Overseas Borrowing as Debt Burden Rises
item.description: Gabon plans to raise about $2 billion on international markets next year to help finance its budget and refinance maturing debt, underscoring the government’s continued reliance on external borrowing even after a recent audit lowered its estimate of outstanding debt.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije

item.title: Stocks, Bonds Climb as Oil Falls on US-Iran Hopes
item.description: Stocks and bonds kicked off the week on a positive note as hopes for diplomatic efforts to end the war in Iran drove oil prices lower, easing inflation anxiety. The advance in equities erased the S&P 500’s decline for the month, with a renewed rally in chipmakers also buoying sentiment. Omar Aguilar, CEO and CIO of Schwab Asset Management, joins for a broad look across asset classes for the rest of 2026. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Paramount Set to Settle Lawsuits, Clearing Way for Warner Bros. Deal
item.description: Paramount Skydance Corp. has reached a settlement with California and other states that were suing to stop its proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc., according to a person familiar with the matter. Talks took place over the weekend. The official deal is expected to be announced Monday. Bloomberg's Chris Palmeri reports from Los Angeles. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AMD, Intel Soar as Meta’s Muse AI Agent Spurs Chip Stock Rally
item.description: Semiconductor stocks soared Monday as early signs of success for Meta Platforms Inc.’s new artificial intelligence agent sparked a wave of enthusiasm around demand for the chips needed to power such agents.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Reinicke

item.title: Russia Set to Extend Diesel Export Ban Beyond End-September
item.description: Russia is set to extend a ban on most diesel exports beyond the end of September as Ukraine continues to attack its refineries, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: AMC Is Overhauling Billions in Debt After Box Office Wins
item.description: AMC Entertainment Holdings Inc. is seeking to raise almost $4 billion of debt to overhaul much of its capital structure, seizing on a box-office recovery to lure investors.
item.dc:creator: Eliza Ronalds-Hannon

item.title: Meta, Tech Stocks Push Indexes Higher as Oil Prices Slide
item.description: Strength in the tech sector spurred US stock benchmarks to extend gains midday Monday as oil prices slide and officials signaled optimism about a summit between US President Donald Trump and China’s Xi Jinping this week.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: EM Assets Gain as Oil Drops, US-China Talks Boost Risk Sentiment
item.description: Emerging-market equities and currencies gained after the US and China gave upbeat assessments of their talks ahead of a summit, while declining oil prices added to positive sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Prima Wirayani, Andras Gergely and Beatriz Amat

item.title: Copper Climbs Toward Record High on Signs of Near-Term Tightness
item.description: Copper extended gains — climbing back toward a record high set earlier this month — as stock markets rallied and there were signs of tightening supply conditions in China.
item.dc:creator: Annie Lee and Mark Burton

item.title: Gold Edges Lower as Traders Weigh Oil Prices and Fed Rate Path
item.description: Gold slipped as investors weighed the risk of a series of further US Federal Reserve rate hikes, even as benchmark oil futures extended a decline.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie, Jack Ryan and Yvonne Yue Li

item.title: Stocks Get Tech Lift as Oil Falls on US-Iran Hopes: Markets Wrap
item.description: A rally in technology giants sent stocks toward their best day since early August, with the market also gaining as hopes for diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war sank oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 21
item.description: Oil fell below $100, heading for its longest run of declines since June, as robust flows through the Strait of Hormuz and diplomacy around the US-Iran war tamed a recent rally.
item.dc:creator: Alex Longley, Bingyan Wang and Nathan Risser

item.title: State Street Sees Resilience Driving Portfolios (Correct)
item.description: State Street Investment Management CEO Yie-Hsin Hung says investors have entered an era where resilient portfolios are increasingly important as higher capital costs, geopolitical tensions and technological change create a wider range of potential outcomes. Hung tells Bloomberg This Weekend hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that institutional investors are adding liquidity and other portfolio buffers, while State Street is also expanding access to private markets and providing the default ETF for the US government's Trump Accounts program. They speak at the 2026 Qatar Economic Forum, UNGA Special Edition; Powered by Bloomberg. (Corrects title of guest in graphic) (Source: Bloomberg)
